title: Welcome — Better Menstrual & Female Health
summary: Small daily changes can support menstrual comfort and overall female health.
details: This guide collects practical, evidence-informed tips covering nutrition, lifestyle, self-care, when to seek care, and emotional wellbeing. Use them as supportive ideas, and consult a clinician for medical concerns.

title: Stay Hydrated
summary: Drink enough water to reduce bloating and help circulation.
details: Aim for consistent hydration throughout the day. Water helps reduce water retention and assists nutrient transport. Add lemon or cucumber for variety.

title: Eat Iron-rich Foods
summary: Help prevent fatigue and support blood levels.
details: Include heme iron (lean red meat, fish, poultry) and non-heme iron (legumes, tofu, spinach). Pair non-heme iron with vitamin C (citrus, bell peppers) to boost absorption.

title: Fiber for Gut & Hormones
summary: A fiber-rich diet supports healthy digestion and hormone balance.
details: Whole grains, vegetables, fruits, beans, and seeds help regulate estrogen metabolism and support a healthy microbiome.

title: Limit Excess Salt
summary: Reduce bloating and water retention by watching sodium intake.
details: Cut back on processed and packaged foods high in salt. Use herbs, lemon, and spices for flavor instead.

title: Reduce Refined Sugar
summary: High sugar can worsen inflammation and mood swings.
details: Prefer whole fruits for sweetness, choose less-processed snacks, and limit sugary drinks which can spike blood sugar and inflammation.

title: Include Healthy Fats
summary: Support hormone production with omega-3 and monounsaturated fats.
details: Fatty fish, walnuts, chia, flaxseed, avocado and olive oil can reduce menstrual pain and support overall hormone health.

title: Moderate Caffeine
summary: Caffeine can increase breast tenderness and worsen anxiety for some people.
details: Try limiting coffee or switch to lower-caffeine options around the luteal/period days if you notice sensitivity.

title: Limit Alcohol
summary: Alcohol can disrupt sleep and increase PMS symptoms for some people.
details: Reducing alcohol intake, especially in the premenstrual and menstrual phase, often helps mood and sleep quality.

title: Regular Gentle Exercise
summary: Movement reduces cramps and improves mood.
details: Walking, yoga, light strength work or gentle cardio help circulation and ease menstrual discomfort. Tailor intensity by cycle phase.

title: Prioritize Sleep
summary: Good sleep supports hormonal balance and mood.
details: Aim for consistent sleep schedules, a cool dark room, and wind-down routines. Poor sleep worsens cravings and symptoms.

title: Support Gut Health
summary: A healthy microbiome supports hormone processing.
details: Fermented foods (yogurt, kefir, sauerkraut) and a fiber-rich diet help maintain beneficial gut bacteria.

title: When to Seek Care
summary: See a clinician if symptoms are severe or changing.
details: If menstrual pain is disabling, bleeding is very heavy, cycles change suddenly, or other symptoms are concerning, consult a healthcare professional.

title: Track Your Cycle
summary: Understanding your cycle helps predict symptoms and identify changes.
details: Use a simple calendar, app, or journal to log bleeding, moods, cramps, sleep, and energy. Patterns help you prepare and speak with clinicians.

title: Warmth Eases Cramps
summary: A warm compress can relieve menstrual cramping.
details: Apply a heat pack or warm water bottle to the lower abdomen for 15–20 minutes. Gentle abdominal massage can also help.

title: Gentle Stretching
summary: Stretching helps release pelvic tension.
details: Yoga poses like child's pose, cat-cow, and gentle twists improve circulation and reduce discomfort during your period.

title: Mindful Breathing
summary: Controlled breathing reduces pain perception and anxiety.
details: Practice a 4-4-6 breathing pattern: inhale 4s, hold 4s, exhale 6s for several minutes when you feel tense or in pain.

title: Omega-3 Supplements
summary: Omega-3s may reduce menstrual pain for some people.
details: Discuss adding a fish oil or algal omega-3 supplement with a clinician if you have heavy cramps or inflammation concerns.

title: Magnesium for Muscle Relaxation
summary: Magnesium can ease cramps and improve mood.
details: Foods rich in magnesium include spinach, nuts, seeds, and whole grains. Oral magnesium supplements can help but check dose and safety first.

title: Maintain a Balanced Plate
summary: A mix of protein, fiber, and good fats stabilizes energy and mood.
details: Build meals with protein (eggs, legumes), fiber (vegetables, whole grains), and healthy fats (avocado, olive oil) for steadier energy across your cycle.

title: Plan for Period Days
summary: Prepare a small kit for comfort and emergencies.
details: Include favorite products, spare underwear, pain relief if appropriate, a heating patch, and a small snack to stay comfortable away from home.

title: Eat Small, Frequent Meals
summary: Smaller meals help reduce nausea and cravings.
details: If you experience digestive upset or low energy, try eating balanced snacks and small meals throughout the day rather than big heavy meals.
